cards.explanation: The answer is that they saw His signs on the sick. John 6:2 says a large crowd followed Him "…because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick." That's the reason the text gives. Signs on the sick, and the crowd followed. I think I'd have been right there with them, friends.

The answer is test. John 6:6 says it plainly: "…He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do." The question wasn't because Jesus was stuck. He already knew what He was about to do. I think Philip was in for a surprise.

The answer is False. The money doesn't stretch that far. Philip, one of Jesus' disciples, says in John 6:7, "Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece." Not a full portion. Not even a small piece for each person.

The answer is True. Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, says, "Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?" (John 6:9). He spots what's on hand, then says out loud how small it looks next to that crowd. I think anybody would have asked the same thing. Hold onto that question, friends, because it gets answered.

The answer is as much as they wanted. John 6:11 says Jesus gave thanks and distributed to those seated "…as much as they wanted." Five thousand men, and nobody got a ration. Then verse 12 says everyone was full. Philip's math about a small piece didn't get the last word.

The answer is wasted. Jesus says, "Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted." (John 6:12). Everybody's already full, and He still tells His disciples to gather what's left. They collect the pieces and fill twelve baskets.

The answer is that this is the Prophet who is to come. After they see the sign, the people begin to say, "Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world." (John 6:14). They'd just seen Jesus distribute five barley loaves and two small fish to those seated as much as they wanted. I think that'd get my attention too, friends. And there's more to come in this story.

The answer is that He withdraws to a mountain by Himself. John 6:15 says Jesus realized they were about to come and make Him king by force, so He "…withdrew again to a mountain by Himself." The crowd wanted to crown Him, and He walked away from it. The text doesn't tell us why He chose that. It just tells us what He did.

The answer is False. The text says the disciples got into a boat and started across the sea, and "…Jesus had not yet gone out to them." (John 6:17). He wasn't in the boat when they set out. Back in verse 15, He had withdrawn to a mountain by Himself.

The answer is True. John 6:19 says they saw Jesus "…approaching the boat, walking on the sea…" and they were terrified. It was dark, the wind was strong, and then somebody comes walking toward you over the water. Friends, I'd have dropped my oar and probably my apron too. They had every reason to be rattled.

The answer is that He tells them it's Him and not to be afraid. Jesus speaks up: "It is I; do not be afraid." (John 6:20). He tells them who it is and tells them not to be afraid. That's what He says to men in a dark boat who were terrified.

The answer is that they take Him in and land at once. John 6:21 says, "Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading." They were willing to take Him in, and the boat reached the shore at once. After all that rowing, I'd call that a nice finish, friends.
